contract: the DVD subpicture cases whose FFmpeg result depends on the target, decoded and folded as subtitle-dvd decodes and folds them: cases the reference flags because they reach a C library result that differs between 32-bit ARM and AArch64 for the same arguments (harness/reference_subtitles_host.h)
each case is pinned per target from that target's own reference run, with the reference's flag; a case passes when the candidate, the reference and the target's pin agree
the decoder follows FFmpeg built with GCC for armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf; where FFmpeg for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu gives another result, the case is open there as a deliberate divergence
preparation outside the timed operation: open the input, select the subpicture stream and its configuration, and copy its packets in demux order

one timed operation: create and open the decoder with the stream's configuration, packet time base and options (a decoder that refuses to open folds as no subtitles and the word 2^64 - 1 in both workers), decode every prepared packet with one call each, drain, fold every output subtitle and free it, free the decoder
pending_module_requirements: a deliberate divergence, target-dependent by design: FFmpeg built for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu decodes the palette option's 1122334455, a number beyond 32 bits, as its low bits (0x334455), where FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM gives 0xffffff; the decoder follows 32-bit ARM

a deliberate divergence, target-dependent by design: FFmpeg built for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu reads the size: width 4294968016, beyond int's range, as its low 32 bits and opens a 720x480 canvas, where FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM refuses to open the decoder; the decoder follows 32-bit ARM

a deliberate divergence, target-dependent by design: FFmpeg built for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu reads the size: height -4294966816, beyond int's range, as its low 32 bits and opens a 720x480 canvas, where FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM refuses to open the decoder; the decoder follows 32-bit ARM

a deliberate divergence, target-dependent by design: FFmpeg built for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu reads delay: fields beyond int's range as their low 32 bits, where FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM saturates them at int's range, so the subtitles are shown at other times there; the decoder follows 32-bit ARM
